PullRequest.Title: sessions: configure external session application badges
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- add a default-off, experiment-controlled `sessions.list.externalApplicationBadge` setting with `off`, `title`, and `details` placements
- add an advanced, experiment-controlled `sessions.list.externalApplicationBadge.showFrom` setting for the optional `From` prefix
- show badges only for external sessions created outside VS Code
- emit the shared `experimentTrigger` event when the first eligible row renders; emit the prefix trigger only while a visible badge mode is active
- hide title badges whenever row actions appear on hover, keyboard focus, onboarding, or phone layouts
- preserve row height across badge, hover, and focus states
- include the creating application in the accessible row label whenever either visible badge mode is enabled
- cover title, details, prefix, hover, focus, light, dark, and high-contrast states with component fixtures

## Testing

- `npm run compile` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- targeted ESLint and stylelint — passed (stylelint reports three pre-existing design-token suggestions)
- sessions contribution tests — 8 passing
- focused sessions-list placement, hover, and trigger tests — 3 passing
- Component Explorer screenshots — visually approved for title, details, no-prefix, hover, focus, long-label truncation, light, dark, and high-contrast states; all 16 previously failing Automations and Blocked Sessions fixtures render cleanly
- `npm run hygiene` — blocked before source checks by the existing Windows URL-path issue resolving `remote/package.json` as `C:\C:\...\remote\package.json`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The eager allocations and listeners are directly visible in the changed template code, and the full-history rendering path is explicit in Automations history. Actual user history lengths vary, which limits severity, but not confidence in the linear mechanism or critical-path reachability.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, DOM event listeners, and per-row reactive computations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added template work grows linearly with every simultaneously rendered session row; Automations history sizes each date-group SessionsFlatList to its full content height, so all N historical runs render rather than only viewport rows.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous view-render latency and retained DOM/listener memory for long session or automation histories.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, session-row templates did not allocate application-badge DOM, badge mouse listeners, or a badge autorun.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every SessionItemRenderer template now eagerly appends two badge spans and installs mouseenter/mouseleave handlers, and every rendered row later gets the badge autorun, even when the new setting is at its default Off value or the session is ineligible/internal.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1359 unconditionally appends `.session-external-application-badge` for every row template; adjacent added lines 1361-1366 add another span and two listeners regardless of badge mode or eligibility.
Findings.Title: Create application badges only when they can be shown
Findings.Impact: Opening Automations with a long run history now synchronously creates and retains 2N hidden badge DOM nodes, 2N listeners, and N reactive computations although badges are default-off. Automations history explicitly lays each group out to its full content height and the run projection has no client-side limit, so months of runs can make this extra work scale into slower view opening and higher memory use.
Findings.Evidence: The changed renderTemplate lines unconditionally append the title badge and its label and register two listeners. renderSession also unconditionally adds the badge autorun. In automationsView.ts, layoutSessionList uses getContentHeight() and calls list.layout(height, width), while SessionsFlatList.getContentHeight() sums every row, making the tree render all history rows; AgentHostAutomationStore._projectRuns() projects all catalog runs without a client cap.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the stable row template lightweight and lazily create/dispose the title badge and its hover handling from the badge autorun only when an eligible row is in Title mode (or delegate hover handling at the list container), so Off/ineligible rows retain no badge-specific DOM or listeners.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, render, scroll, hover, or focus the main Sessions list with internal and external sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tree row template creation and renderSession run synchronously before visible rows appear; badge hover setup is also synchronous, while delayed hover display is off the initial critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue an `experimentTrigger` telemetry event through ITelemetryService for the badge-mode and, when visible, show-from treatments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per treatment per window/process after shared telemetry deduplication, although local configuration inspection occurs on each reporting callback invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two badge experiment trigger events and their configuration inspections did not occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only synchronous configuration inspection and telemetry enqueue are on row-render/ARIA recomputation; transport is not awaited and does not block list progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of rendered/overscanned viewport rows, not the full session collection; badge eligibility and label work additionally scale with rendered external non-VS-Code sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rows render sequentially on the UI thread; there is no limiter or asynchronous batching in the changed badge work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values are local observables and update on relevant configuration changes. Experiment telemetry is cold once per treatment per telemetry service, then coalesced by the shared WeakMap/Set; no negative-cache behavior applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed template and autorun code directly establish synchronous per-rendered-row DOM, listener, observable, and label work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport row count and external-session prevalence vary; the main virtualized list bounds simultaneous row work, so its added cost alone is small.
Scenarios.Verdict: The main list remains virtualized and telemetry is globally deduplicated, but the unconditional default-off row-template allocations contribute to the reported eager-work regression when the same renderer is used by unvirtualized flat-list surfaces.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Automations history containing many completed run sessions across date groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AutomationHistorySection synchronously creates one SessionsFlatList per date group, sets all sessions, computes full content height, and lays each list out at that height; every historical row therefore constructs its complete SessionItemRenderer template before the history is displayed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is all N resolved historical run sessions, because each group list is laid out to its summed content height; AgentHostAutomationStore projects all catalog and archived runs without a client-side display cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Date groups and rows are built sequentially on the UI thread with no virtualization across the overall history and no yielding/backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent date groups retain their row trees and the newly added badge DOM/listeners while active, avoiding rebuilds on unchanged rerenders but retaining O(N) resources. Badge configuration observables are local and telemetry remains globally deduplicated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: full-height list layout, uncapped client projection, unconditional template allocations, and retention through persistent groups are all explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The host may bound catalog history outside the inspected client code, and user run counts vary; the client path itself applies no cap, so months of scheduled runs are a realistic scaling input.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity eager work: the default-off feature adds two hidden DOM nodes, two listeners, and a reactive computation to every fully rendered history row.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the blocked-sessions surface backed by SessionsFlatList
Scenarios.CriticalPath: BlockedSessionsList constructs a flat list and synchronously renders the supplied blocked session rows before laying out the context surface.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially enqueue the same experiment-trigger telemetry events when an eligible external blocked row first renders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event for each of two treatments per telemetry service after deduplication, shared with the main list and Automation lists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No external-application badge treatment event was emitted from blocked-session rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The event is not awaited; only synchronous enqueue/config inspection is on the render path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cardinality is the current blocked-session count, ordinarily small and naturally constrained by active sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous sequential UI rendering; no async boundaries or burst concurrency were introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rows and their badge resources live with the popover/list and are disposed together; telemetry uses the same per-window treatment deduplication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed row path; low uncertainty only in typical row count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Blocked-session counts are expected to remain low, so the added per-row resources are unlikely to create standalone visible degradation here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this surface reaches the same eager allocations but has a small realistic collection size and proper disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change external application badge placement or prefix settings while session lists are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration event synchronously invalidates the observables; observed row autoruns and ARIA-label derivations recompute and update DOM before the UI settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Placement updates scale with rendered rows observing the mode; title/prefix label updates scale with rendered eligible external rows. In full-height Automation flat lists, ARIA mode observers can span all rendered rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable fanout on the UI thread with no batching beyond observable invalidation semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm telemetry calls are deduplicated after local configuration inspection. Configuration values are recomputed from the local service on relevant events; no remote read is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that fanout occurs; magnitude is low because setting changes are infrequent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users rarely toggle these experimental settings and experiment-default update frequency is unclear, limiting practical impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: recomputation is event-driven and infrequent; the material issue is the unconditional retained template work already reported.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced main Sessions, Automation history, blocked-session, setting-change, hover/focus, accessibility, and experiment-trigger paths. Submitted one low-severity eager-work finding for default-off badge DOM/listener/reactive allocations scaling across fully rendered Automation history. Telemetry boundaries are globally deduplicated and no subprocess, filesystem, database, or network critical-path fanout was introduced.
